segments.text: In 1835, a newspaper reported bat-people on the Moon.

image.file: File:Lunar animals and other objects Discovered by Sir John Herschel in his observatory at the Cape of Good Hope and copied from sketches in the Edinburgh Journal of Science. LCCN2003665049.jpg

visual.label: Lithograph sold by The Sun, 1835 (Library of Congress)

segments.text: New York's Sun ran the story on its front page.
The source? Sir John Herschel, a real astronomer working in South Africa.

image.file: File:Julia Margaret Cameron - John Herschel (Metropolitan Museum of Art copy, restored).jpg

segments.text: The paper claimed his new telescope could see life on the Moon.

image.file: File:'Site of the Twenty Feet Reflector at Feldhausen. Cape of Good Hope Sept 1834' RMG PU1906.tiff

visual.label: Herschel's actual observatory at the Cape of Good Hope, 1834

segments.text: First came unicorns, and beavers that walked on two legs.
On day four: humans with bat wings.

visual.label: A "man-bat", Italian edition of the story, 1836

segments.text: Believers and skeptics alike rushed to read the next part.

image.file: File:Lunar animals and other objects Discovered by Sir John Herschel in his observatory at the Cape of Good Hope and copied from sketches in the Edinburgh Journal of Science. LCCN2003665049.jpg

segments.text: Herschel himself didn't hear about it until long after.

image.file: File:Julia Margaret Cameron - John Herschel (Metropolitan Museum of Art copy, restored).jpg

segments.text: Historians generally credit a Sun writer, Richard Adams Locke.

visual.evidence: The Moon Hoax, 1859 reprint naming Locke

segments.text: And The Sun? It never took the story back.

title: In 1835, a newspaper reported bat-people on the Moon #history
description: In August 1835, The Sun of New York claimed that astronomer John Herschel had spotted unicorns, two-legged beavers and winged people on the Moon. Historians credit the hoax to writer Richard Adams Locke, and the paper never retracted it.
sources: Library of Congress, Folklife Today, "The Great Moon Hoax" (August 2014): https://blogs.loc.gov/folklife/2014/08/the-great-moon-hoax/
Linda Hall Library, Scientist of the Day, "Richard Adams Locke": https://www.lindahall.org/about/news/scientist-of-the-day/richard-adams-locke
